title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text: Automation requires repeatable runs that reuse a stable output root, yet the current pipeline backs up existing task directories on the first encounter per process. The proposed autocleaneeg-pipeline serve workflow introduces a dedicated, self-contained automation workspace with explicit test/live separation and managed runtime installs. This document extends the original idempotency analysis to incorporate that workspace concept, clarify command semantics, and define a configuration governance model that preserves uptime, auditability, and reproducible outputs.

title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text: Automation requires repeatable runs that reuse a stable output root, yet the current pipeline backs up existing task directories on the first encounter per process. The proposed autocleaneeg-pipeline serve workflow introduces a dedicated, self-contained automation workspace with explicit test/live separation and managed runtime installs. This document extends the original idempotency analysis to incorporate that workspace concept, clarify command semantics, and define a configuration governance model that preserves uptime, auditability, and reproducible outputs.

title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text:
Current Backup Mechanism
The backup trigger lives in step_prepare_directories, where an existing task root is moved to a timestamped backup directory before new BIDS-compliant subdirectories are created. The behavior is invoked by Pipeline during every run, and any backup event is captured in the database metadata as directory_backup, then used by resolve_moved_path in src/autoclean/utils/path_resolution.py to repair legacy paths. The net effect is that every new CLI invocation generates a fresh output root, which is ideal for safety but unsuitable for automation workflows that must append artifacts to a single target.





flowchart LR
  A[Existing task root] --> B{First encounter
in process?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Move to task_backup_timestamp]
  B -->|No| D[Reuse task root]
  C --> D
  D --> E[Create/ensure BIDS, reports, exports, QA]


 Figure 1. Task-root backup flow during directory preparation.

title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text:
Serve Workspace Architecture
The serve workflow introduces a distinct automation workspace that is self-contained and deliberately structured to maintain separation between test and live operations. Within this folder, runtimes/test and runtimes/live host isolated pipeline runtimes, while serve-test.yaml and serve-live.yaml live at the workspace root for operator edits. Each automation workspace under the parent folder is named using the taskfile-montage-version convention to make provenance explicit and to align with the stated requirement that a task file plus montage uniquely define an automation instance.





flowchart TD
  A[serve-workspace/] --> B[runtimes/]
  B --> C[test/]
  B --> D[live/]
  A --> E[serve-test.yaml]
  A --> F[serve-live.yaml]
  A --> G[deploy/validated-yaml]
  A --> H[taskfile-montage-version/]


 Figure 2. Proposed autocleaneeg-serve workspace layout. 




Table 1. Serve workspace components and responsibilities.







Component
Purpose
Notes




runtimes/test
Isolated test runtime installation
Enables safe validation without disrupting live runs.


runtimes/live
Production runtime installation
Serves active workloads with pinned versions.


serve-test.yaml
Operator-facing test configuration
Edited directly; validated before deployment.


serve-live.yaml
Operator-facing live configuration
Edited directly; validated before deployment.


deploy/
Hidden deployed YAMLs
Replaced only after validation passes.


taskfile-montage-version/
Automation workspace
Contains per-automation task outputs and logs.

title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text:
Command Family and Governance
The autocleaneeg-pipeline serve command family acts as the automation manager. It must accept either an existing serve workspace path or create a new one, then provide a consistent set of control verbs so operators can manage configuration, validation, and deployment without manual file shuffling.

Table 2. Serve command family expectations.







Command
Purpose
Expected Behavior




serve workspace
Set or edit serve workspace
Creates or updates the active automation workspace pointer.


serve list
Enumerate automations
Lists test/live configurations and workspace status.


serve validate
Dry-run config validation
Runs against test or live config without deployment.


serve deploy
Promote validated config
Replaces hidden deployed YAML and activates runtime.









NoteConfiguration Safety



Live uptime requires that serve-test.yaml and serve-live.yaml are never used directly by automation. The system should validate these files, then atomically replace hidden deployed YAMLs in the deploy/ path to avoid partial or invalid updates.

title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text:
Workspace Lifecycle and Deployment Workflow
The serve workspace must support a predictable lifecycle that separates operator edits, validation, and deployment while keeping the runtime isolation intact. The workflow below formalizes how the automation manager should create or attach to a workspace, validate YAML updates, and promote them into the hidden deployed set used by the automation engine.





flowchart TD
  A[User selects or creates serve workspace] --> B[Initialize runtimes/test and runtimes/live]
  B --> C[Edit serve-test.yaml or serve-live.yaml]
  C --> D[serve validate (dry-run)]
  D -->|Pass| E[Promote to deploy/hidden YAML]
  D -->|Fail| F[Reject and report errors]
  E --> G[serve deploy activates runtime]


 Figure 3. Serve workspace lifecycle and deployment flow.

title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text:
YAML Configuration Intent
The serve YAML files encode runtime selection, ingestion boundaries, and the taskfile/montage combinations used to derive automation workspace names. The intent is to minimize operator input while preserving rigorous controls over what the automation engine executes. Ingestion folders should explicitly avoid partially staged data, and the runtime path should point to the intended autocleaneeg executable within the test or live runtime tree.
runtime: runtimes/live
mode: live
ingestion_folders:
  - /data/inbox/live
  - /data/inbox/archive
workspace_name: "taskfile-montage-version"
taskfile: RestingEyesOpen
montage: standard_1020
The listing above illustrates the minimal schema elements implied by the user requirements, emphasizing runtime selection, ingestion boundaries, and the taskfile/montage pairing that drives workspace naming. Any implementation must ensure that the deployed YAML is versioned and that updates are atomic after validation.

title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text:
Downstream Artifacts Affected
Disabling backups changes how several output families accumulate across runs. The core directories are created under the task root, and many downstream tools assume those paths are stable. The table below summarizes the primary artifacts affected if backups are skipped.

Table 3. Output artifacts affected by disabling task-root backups.







Artifact/Directory
Examples
Impact When Backups Are Disabled




bids/derivatives
Cleaned data, staged FIF/SET files
Files may be overwritten if naming is deterministic; may need run-scoped subfolders.


reports/
PDF QA reports, summaries
Reports accumulate; repeated run outputs may need versioning.


exports/
Final exported datasets
Overwrite risk if filenames repeat; automation should define overwrite policy.


ica/
ICA FIF caches, component notes
Cache reuse may be beneficial but needs collision awareness.


qa/
QA images and metrics
Re-runs can append; consider run identifier in filenames.


status/
run_id.json markers
Task-level markers can be overwritten; run-level markers remain additive.


pipeline.db
Run metadata, audit log
Single DB becomes authoritative; must remain append-only for compliance.

title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text:
Toggle Options and Automation Mode
A surgical toggle should avoid global behavior changes while enabling automation use cases. The most constrained options are (a) a CLI or API flag that disables the backup only for a single run, or (b) reusing the existing workspace.auto_backup configuration as a feature flag. The latter already defaults to True in src/autoclean/utils/config.py and is enforced during setup, so a new automation command could temporarily set it to False for an isolated run without altering user defaults.

Table 4. Candidate toggle mechanisms for automation mode.








Option
Scope
Pros
Risks




CLI flag --automation
Per-run
Minimal blast radius; explicit intent
Must be propagated through CLI → Pipeline → step_prepare_directories.


Config override workspace.auto_backup
Workspace
Aligns with existing config model
Needs guardrails to avoid accidental permanent disable.


Environment variable AUTOCLEAN_AUTOMATION=1
Session
Easy for automation scripts
Less discoverable; must be documented.









NoteRecommendation



Use a per-run automation flag that sets auto_backup=False only for that invocation, leaving the default safety posture intact. This supports the proposed autocleaneeg serve workflow without permanently altering workspace configuration.

title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text:
First-Step Plan

Introduce a serve workspace registry that records the active automation root and enforces the test/live runtime layout.
Define a single automation entry point (autocleaneeg-pipeline serve) that carries an automation_mode flag through the CLI, Pipeline, and step_prepare_directories.
Add configuration validation that promotes operator YAMLs into hidden deployed YAMLs only after dry-run checks succeed.
Document an overwrite policy for artifact families (reports, exports, derivatives) and recommend run-scoped filenames where collisions are likely.
Add an audit note to run metadata explaining that automation mode preserved the existing task root.

title: RFC 002: Automation Idempotency Preparation
text:
Discussion: Idempotency and Run Coexistence
Idempotency requires that a run can be repeated without corrupting or fragmenting outputs. Skipping the backup restores folder stability but raises overwrite risks for deterministic filenames. The safest mitigation is to append run_id or timestamp suffixes for files that are not inherently append-only, while leaving database and status logging as append-only records. Test/live separation inside the serve workspace provides an additional safety valve: validation runs can exercise the exact runtime and config layout without touching production outputs, and deployment only proceeds when validation results are clean.

title: Executed Document: RFC 001 - Introduction to AutoCleanEEG Pipeline
text:
This document executes the instruction to write an introduction to the big picture of what AutoCleanEEG Pipeline is.



Based on the codebase exploration, AutoCleanEEG Pipeline is a modular framework for automated EEG data processing. Key components include:

Core pipeline orchestration
Modular processing functions (preprocessing, ICA, epoching, artifacts)
Plugin system for file formats
CLI interface
Task configuration system
BIDS support
Built-in tasks for various paradigms




AutoCleanEEG Pipeline is a comprehensive, automated framework for EEG data preprocessing that streamlines the complex process of cleaning and preparing electroencephalography (EEG) data for analysis. Built on the robust MNE-Python library, it offers a modular “lego block” approach that allows users to construct customized preprocessing pipelines tailored to their specific experimental paradigms and data characteristics.
The pipeline supports a wide range of EEG paradigms including Auditory Steady-State Response (ASSR), Mismatch Negativity (MMN), resting state, and more, making it versatile for both research and clinical applications. Its design emphasizes research workflows, BIDS compatibility for standardized data organization, and detailed quality control outputs to ensure data integrity.



Modular Architecture: Processing steps are provided as interchangeable blocks, allowing flexible pipeline construction without coding.
Automated Quality Assurance: Built-in artifact detection, channel rejection, and epoch quality flagging with statistical methods.
BIDS Compliance: Standard data organization and metadata handling for reproducible research.
Extensible System: Plugin architecture for custom file formats and processing steps.
Batch Processing: Efficient handling of multiple files with parallel execution and database logging.
Comprehensive Reporting: PDF reports, visualizations, and metadata summaries for transparency.
Task System: Pre-configured tasks for common paradigms with customizable parameters.




The pipeline is designed for neuroscientists, clinicians, and data analysts who need reliable, reproducible EEG preprocessing. It serves:

Researchers: Automate routine preprocessing to focus on scientific questions
Clinicians: Standardize processing for consistent clinical EEG analysis

Developers: Extensible framework for custom EEG processing tools




AutoCleanEEG fits into the EEG processing workflow as the preprocessing stage, taking raw EEG data and producing clean, analysis-ready datasets. It bridges the gap between data acquisition and statistical analysis, ensuring data quality while reducing manual processing time.
By automating routine cleaning tasks, it allows researchers to focus on their scientific questions while maintaining high standards of data quality and processing transparency.
